answer: Tide-bridge thread grafting: each agent carries a persistent hash thread chaining its prior actions. To spawn a clone, the origin must graft a new thread onto its own, consuming a scarce daily graft budget and inheriting the parent's full liability history. Clones share lineage exposure, so one clone's fraud slashes the parent's reachable counterparties. Marginal clone EV: graft cost plus diluted trust plus inherited fraud risk exceeds any per-clone gain.
